\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter03.LearningTheory.FourierEstimation}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Rational Fourier observation]
\lean{FABL.rationalFourierObservation}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b002,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b004
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003}
\label{FABL.rationalFourierObservation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be finite, and let $(x,y)$
be a labeled example with $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$ and $y\in\{−1,1\}$. Its rational Fourier
observation on $S$ is $y\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Fourier observation]
\lean{FABL.fourierObservation}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b002,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b004
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p025-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003
}
\label{FABL.fourierObservation}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.monomial}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be finite, and let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$. The Fourier
observation of $f$ at $x$ on $S$ is $f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Rational and real Fourier observations]
\lean{FABL.rationalFourierObservation_cast}
\label{FABL.rationalFourierObservation_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierObservation, FABL.monomial, FABL.rationalFourierObservation, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f$ be a sign-valued function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x$ be a point of that cube. The
rational observation formed from the label $f(x)$ and the product of the coordinates
indexed by $S$, when regarded as a real number, equals the real-valued Fourier
observation of $f$ at $x$ for $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Empirical Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p010-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003}
\label{FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.Sign, FABL.rationalFourierObservation}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be finite, and let
$m\in\mathbb N$. Given $m$ labeled examples $(x_j,y_j)$ in $\{−1,1\}^n\times\{−1,1\}$,
the empirical Fourier coefficient on $S$ is $\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=0}^{m-1} y_j\prod_{i\in
S}(x_j)_i$, with the expression understood as the rational sum divided by $m$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Real empirical Fourier coefficient]
\lean{FABL.realEmpiricalFourierCoeff}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p010-b002}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003}
\label{FABL.realEmpiricalFourierCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.fourierObservation}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be finite, and let $m\in\mathbb N$. For a batch
$x_0,\ldots,x_{m-1}$ of cube inputs, the real empirical Fourier coefficient on $S$ is
$\frac{1}{m}\sum_{j=0}^{m-1} f(x_j)\prod_{i\in S}(x_j)_i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Agreement of empirical Fourier coefficients]
\lean{FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff_cast}
\label{FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff_cast}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff, FABL.rationalFourierObservation_cast, FABL.realEmpiricalFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ and $m$ be natural numbers, let $f$ be a function from the sign cube
$\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to the signs, let $S$ be a subset of the $n$ coordinates, and let
$x_1,\ldots,x_m$ be sign vectors in the cube. The rational empirical Fourier coefficient
computed from the labeled samples $(x_i,f(x_i))$, viewed as a real number, equals the
real empirical Fourier coefficient of $f$ on these inputs.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Fourier coefficient estimator program]
\lean{FABL.fourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p010-b001,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p010-b002,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p010-b003
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003
}
\label{FABL.fourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ be finite, and let
$m\in\mathbb N$. The random-example learning program draws a batch of $m$ independent
uniform labeled examples, returns their empirical Fourier coefficient on $S$ as a
rational number, and charges $m(|S|+1)$ local computation steps.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Scheduled Fourier coefficient estimator]
\lean{FABL.scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003
}
\label{FABL.scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.LearningProgram, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.fourierCoeffEstimatorProgram, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount}
For a finite set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ and rational parameters
$\varepsilon,\delta\in(0,1/2]$, the scheduled Fourier coefficient estimator is the
random-example learning program that runs the Fourier coefficient estimator on $S$ using
the sample count prescribed by $\varepsilon$ and $\delta$, and returns a rational
output.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Law of the Fourier coefficient estimator]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_fourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_fourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff, FABL.fourierCoeffEstimatorProgram, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,m\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$ be a target function, and let
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The estimator's outcome law is obtained by drawing $m$
independent uniform inputs $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\{\pm1\}^n$, returning the empirical
coefficient $\frac1m\sum_{j=1}^m f(x_j)\prod_{i\in S}(x_j)_i$, and recording learning
cost $(m,0,m+m(|S|+1))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Distribution and cost of the scheduled Fourier estimator]
\lean{FABL.runWithCost_scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\label{FABL.runWithCost_scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.empiricalFourierCoeff, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.runWithCost_fourierCoeffEstimatorProgram, FABL.scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $S$ be a finite subset of $\text{Fin}(n)$, and let
$psilon,\delta$ be rational parameters satisfying $0<psilon,\delta\text{ and
}epsilon,\delta\text{ are at most }1/2$. For any Boolean target on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube, the estimator’s run has the distribution obtained by drawing uniformly a
batch of $m$ cube inputs, where $m$ is the prescribed sample count, and returning the
empirical Fourier coefficient of their target labels together with cost
$(m,0,m+m(|S|+1))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Scheduled Fourier estimator cost]
\lean{FABL.scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram_cost_eq}
\label{FABL.scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram_cost_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.LearningCost, FABL.LearningProgram.runWithCost, FABL.PositiveLearningParameter, FABL.fourierEstimatorSampleCount, FABL.runWithCost_scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram, FABL.scheduledFourierCoeffEstimatorProgram}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube
$\\{-1,1\\}^n$, let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$
satisfy $0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. Every outcome in the support of the scheduled
Fourier coefficient estimator, when run on $f$, has cost $(m,0,m+m(|S|+1))$, where
$m=\lceil 2b(\delta)/\varepsilon^2\rceil$ and $b(\delta)=\lceil\log_2\lceil
2/\delta\rceil\rceil$ is the specified failure-bit count.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform product measure]
\lean{FABL.uniformSample_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\label{FABL.uniformSample_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set equipped with a measurable space in which every
singleton is measurable, and let $m$ be a nonnegative integer. The measure associated
with the uniform distribution on the set of functions from $\{1,\ldots,m\}$ to $\Omega$
equals the product, over those $m$ coordinates, of the uniform measure on $\Omega$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Product measure for uniform sample inputs]
\lean{FABL.uniformSampleInputs_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\label{FABL.uniformSampleInputs_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformSample_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\difficulty{1}
For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the measure associated with a uniform random element of
$(\{−1,1\}^n)^m$ is the product, over the $m$ coordinates, of the measures associated
with uniform random elements of $\{−1,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Finite empirical mean]
\lean{FABL.finiteUniformEmpiricalMean}
\label{FABL.finiteUniformEmpiricalMean}
\leanok
Let $$ be a finite nonempty set, let $m$ be a natural number, let $o$ be a
real-valued observation on that set, and let $x_0,\ldots,x_{m-1}$ be a sample
from the set, with repetitions allowed. The finite uniform empirical mean is
$\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=0}^{m-1}o(x_i)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform sample mean concentration]
\lean{FABL.measure_finiteUniformEmpiricalMean_sub_expect_ge_le}
\label{FABL.measure_finiteUniformEmpiricalMean_sub_expect_ge_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.finiteUniformEmpiricalMean, FABL.integral_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.uniformPMF, FABL.uniformSample_toMeasure_eq_pi}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set equipped with a measurable space in which every
singleton is measurable, and let $g:\\Omega\\to\\mathbb R$ take values in $[-1,1]$. For
a positive integer $m$ and $\\varepsilon\\ge0$, choose uniformly an $m$-tuple of
elements of $\\Omega$. The probability that the empirical mean of $g$ on this tuple
differs from the uniform expectation of $g$ on $\\Omega$ by at least $\\varepsilon$ is
at most $2\\exp(-m\\varepsilon^2/2)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Range of a Fourier observation]
\lean{FABL.fourierObservation_mem_Icc}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003}
\label{FABL.fourierObservation_mem_Icc}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierObservation, FABL.monomial_sq, FABL.signValue_eq_neg_one_or_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, let
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. Then $f(x)\prod_{i\in
S}x_i\in[-1,1]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subgaussian Fourier observations]
\lean{FABL.fourierObservation_hasSubgaussianMGF}
\label{FABL.fourierObservation_hasSubgaussianMGF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierObservation, FABL.fourierObservation_mem_Icc, FABL.integral_fourierObservation_uniformPMF, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$, and let
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For a uniformly random $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, put
$X=f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ and $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i]$. The
centered observation $X-\widehat f(S)$ has subgaussian moment generating function with
parameter $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subgaussian bound for a sampled Fourier observation]
\lean{FABL.sampleCoordinate_fourierObservation_hasSubgaussianMGF}
\label{FABL.sampleCoordinate_fourierObservation_hasSubgaussianMGF}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierObservation, FABL.fourierObservation_mem_Icc, FABL.integral_fourierObservation_uniformPMF, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $S$ be a finite subset of $\text{Fin}(n)$, let
$i\in\text{Fin}(m)$, and let the target be a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional
sign cube. Under the product law of $m$ independent uniform cube inputs, the centered
Fourier observation at coordinate $i$ has subgaussian moment-generating-function bound
with parameter $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Centered Fourier observation sum]
\lean{FABL.sum_centeredFourierObservation_eq_mul_sub_realEmpirical}
\label{FABL.sum_centeredFourierObservation_eq_mul_sub_realEmpirical}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierObservation, FABL.realEmpiricalFourierCoeff}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube
$\\{-1,1\\}^n$ to the signs $\\{-1,1\\}$, and let $S$ be a subset of
$\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$. For a positive integer $m$ and a sample $x_1,\\ldots,x_m$ in the
cube, the sum of the centered Fourier observations equals $m$ times the difference
between their empirical average and the Fourier coefficient: $\\sum_{j=1}^m
(f(x_j)\\chi_S(x_j)-\\widehat f(S))=m(\\frac{1}{m}\\sum_{j=1}^m
f(x_j)\\chi_S(x_j)-\\widehat f(S))$, where $\\chi_S$ is the monomial indexed by $S$ and
$\\widehat f(S)$ is the uniform Fourier coefficient.
\end{theorem}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p080-b003}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on the sign cube, let
$S$ be a subset of its coordinates, and let $\varepsilon,\delta\in\mathbb Q$ satisfy
$0<\varepsilon,\delta\le 1/2$. The probability that the scheduled empirical Fourier
coefficient differs from the Fourier coefficient of $f$ on $S$ by at least $\varepsilon$
is at most $\delta$; the error and threshold are measured as real numbers.
\end{theorem}
